why: Non-negative edge weights and 'shortest distance from one source to every vertex' is exactly single-source Dijkstra with a binary heap; the story adds nothing beyond the -1 for unreachable vertices.
hints: Weights differ, so plain BFS no longer finds shortest paths. But they are never negative; which algorithm needs exactly that?
Dijkstra: always settle the unsettled vertex with the smallest tentative distance, then relax its edges. With non-negative weights a settled distance is final.
Adjacency list with both directions per edge, a heap of (dist, vertex), skip stale heap entries whose dist exceeds the recorded one. O((V + E) log V); finally replace infinity with -1.
pitfalls: Add every edge in both directions; the graph is undirected.
Skip stale heap entries (d > dist[u]) or the run degrades badly with many parallel edges.
Zero-weight edges and self-loops are allowed; they must not break relaxation (use strict < when relaxing).
Unreached vertices must be reported as -1, not as a large sentinel.
